description: Shared dependency policy for every firmfooting-owned organisation. Extend it, do not copy it.

packageRules.description: npm waits 14 days like everything else. config:best-practices extends security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, whose package rule sets npm to 3 days and beats the top-level figure; this rule comes later, so it wins. Only minor and patch are named: the preset deliberately clears the wait for update types that carry no release timestamp (pin, bump, lockFileMaintenance and others), where a wait would hold the update forever. Majors get the 30 days below.
Majors soak for a month before they are offered. Longer than the 14 days above on purpose: a major is read by a person, so the wait costs nothing anybody is sitting through.

Anything that is not a major merges itself once CI is green. Renovate will not automerge a branch that has no passing checks, so a repository with no tests merges nothing and this fails safe. It does NOT prove a gate exists: only branch protection does that, and most repositories here have none, several because they are private on a plan that does not offer it. Where the gate matters, add required checks to the repository.
Majors always wait for a person. A major is where an API disappears, a default flips, or a peer range breaks, none of which a green suite reliably catches.

firmfooting/.github's shared workflows skip the release-age wait. They are this organisation's own tags, reviewed before they are cut, so the wait guards against nothing, and it would hold every repository on the previous workflows for two weeks: v1.3.0, which moves the shared jobs to the runners private repositories can still use, would have waited 14 days. Comes last so it also beats the majors rule's 30 days; a major still waits for a person.
